chunks: This is because formality is inseparable from hardship and it is an evil that is caused by a comrade for whom formality is observed. Consequently, he is the worst of all comrades.
ai.seo_question: Why is a companion who demands formal courtesy considered the worst type of friend?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī elucidates that social obligations (taklif) inherently entail hardship (mashaqqah), which is a necessary evil arising from the one who demands it. Consequently, the companion who imposes this burden is deemed the worst among peers, highlighting the relational cost of formal duties in Shia ethical thought.
